messages:
maya: Quick head's up — ran a short smoke on paged + interleaved KV layout and hit a consistent tail latency bump when the KV start offset is not 64-byte aligned. Repro steps and numbers below. :eyes:

sam: can you paste the microprofile and the exact inputs you used?

maya: sure — small model, seq=512, batch=8, dtype=bf16, 4k warmup tokens then 10k steady. Baseline (separate layout): p99=28.4ms. Interleaved with unaligned starts: p99=31.8ms, p95 up ~8%. CPU usage same, GPU %util similar but kernel time increased.

perf-bot: perf summary (striped):
```
kernel: flash_fused_qkv  time_mean=1.9ms  time_p99=6.2ms  calls=1250
kv_store_alignment: 64 -> misaligned in 37% of requests
kv_stride_miss: +12% memory-load-stalls
fallbacks: paged->packed copy triggered for 9% of batches
```

jonathan: Hmm — BF16 vs FP16 matters here. On A100 BF16 memory ops are cheaper but alignment sensitivity differs for fused kernels. Do you still see regression if you force fp16?

maya: Forced fp16 run: p99=30.1ms (better but still worse than separate baseline). So dtype reduces but doesn't eliminate. Looks like misaligned strides cause extra bank conflicts in the paged kernel.

liam: Proposal: pad the KV base pointer to 256B boundary when serving paged/interleaved variant to guarantee 64B-aligned vector loads. Cheap allocator tweak and toggle via runtime flag. Also add heuristic: if (seq % 64 != 0 || dtype==bf16) prefer fused kernel fallback.

sam: Can you sketch the config change? I can microbench a canary.

liam: config snippet to gate (runtime flag):
```
serve.kv.pad_base_bytes = 256  # default 0
serve.kv.interleave_alignment = 64
kernel_selector.prefer_fused_when_unaligned = false
```

maya: i'll wire pad_base_bytes=256 in a canary pool and run the same microbench. If p99 returns to baseline we can land allocator change + add regression test.

perf-bot: canary results posted (after 3k requests): p99=28.6ms, p95=18.2ms, misaligned hits dropped to <1%.

jonathan: nice. We'll also add a kernel-selector tweak: prefer `flash_paged_aligned` variant when alignment known at enqueue-time, otherwise mark request for `flash_fused` to avoid mid-kernel slow paths.

sam: ack, i'll open a tiny PR with allocator pad + selector flag + a microbench test case (seq=512,batch=8,dtype=bf16). PR will include the perf-bot snapshot to hold the regression guard.

maya: thanks team — plan: canary -> perf PR -> enable by default with rollout. Leaving notes for oncall: if latency regresses after rollout, rollback pad_base_bytes and set kernel_selector.prefer_fused_when_unaligned=true. :thumbsup:
